text:
Priya: :wave: Taking over the bridge — quick handoff. We have an active P0 (high tail latency on hosted/generation). Incident bot posted summary below. I'm about to hand drive to Taylor in 5 minutes unless anyone objects.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P0 #4821 - generation-upticks - started 15m ago. Affected: hosted/text-gen endpoint. Error rate up ~3% and 99th latency from 220ms -> 2.1s. Pager routed to eng-oncall.

Sam: TL;DR — rolling restart of a subset of inference pods fixed transient OOM earlier but latency persisted. We've pinned traffic to dedicated pool 'dp-3' via routing fallback. No customer-facing 5xx spikes yet, but user complaints from a customer in EU.

Priya: Owner proposal: Taylor drives, Jordan handles comms. I'll stay secondary for context. Any coverage gaps?

Taylor: I can drive. Taking over now — I'm on the Zoom. Steps I'll run: 1) confirm routing rules, 2) check model variants & quantization fallback, 3) validate KV cache saturation. Jordan you good for comms?

Jordan: Yep I can own comms. I'll post to #incidents-customer-updates and notify the account team for the EU tenant. Draft message: "We're investigating higher than normal generation latency; temporary routing to dedicated pool in place; no data loss; ETA 30-60 mins" — ok?

Sam: Runbook link: <https://internal.redwood/runbooks/p0-generation-latency|runbook/p0-generation-latency>. Key checks: 
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference
redis-cli -h kv-cache-01 INFO memory
curl -sS https://metrics.redwood/api/alerts?incident=4821 | jq .
```

OpsRunbookBot: Reminder: Handoff checklist not complete. Missing: confirm secondary oncall and confirm comms channel. Use `/handoff-ack` when done.

Priya: Secondary confirmed (me). Comms channel: #incidents-customer-updates. I ran quick cache check: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 94% -> 63% over last 20m. Might be churn from many long context requests.

Taylor: Good signal. I'll throttle long-context inference path and enable aggressive prefix caching for the next 15m; if latency drops, we'll keep the policy. Applying routing change now: `POST /api/v1/routing/policy` with body to lower long-context traffic to fallback.

Jordan: Posted initial customer note and pinged account team. Also creating a short status page snippet.

Priya: Thanks. Two coordination points: 1) If latency doesn't improve in 20m, escalate to infra (Ethan) for hardware checks. 2) If error rate >4% switch to canary model variant (v2-quant) and notify comms.

Taylor: Confirmed. I will update thread when routing change applied and after the 10m metric check. Taking driver role now. Priya — thanks for context. Jordan — thanks for comms.

Sam: Leaving the bridge (off shift) — @Taylor you have full driver handoff. OpsRunbookBot: `/handoff-ack Taylor Jordan Priya`

Jordan: :thumbsup: Acknowledged. I'll keep updates concise and timestamped.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: driver=Taylor, comms=Jordan, secondary=Priya, runbook=/runbooks/p0-generation-latency, handoff_ts=1719992345

Taylor: Update 5m after change — 99th latency down to 480ms, KV cache hit-rate back to 87%. Keeping measures for 15m. If stable we'll mark containment and start timeline.

Jordan: Posted containment message to customers and emailed account team. Continuing to monitor.

Priya: Noted. Leaving this thread open until containment confirmed.

Taylor: If anyone joins later, the handoff summary: driver=Taylor, comms=Jordan, secondary=Priya. Primary mitigation was traffic routing + aggressive prefix caching. Escalation path to infra if degradation resumes.

Jordan: Closing note scheduled once 30m stable. :white_check_mark:
